solve:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Determines whether the cake grid can be cut into (H+1)*(V+1) rectangular pieces each containing exactly the same number of '@' chips, and prints POSSIBLE or IMPOSSIBLE for the current test case." solve]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> kase </REF>: int "Current test case number used in the printed output."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Read the first input line, split it into exactly four integer tokens, assign them to R, C, H, and V, and initialize cakes as an empty list. RESULT R,C,H,V,cakes]
            [COMMAND For each row index i from 0 to R-1 inclusive, read one stripped input line, convert it to a list of characters, and append that list to cakes. RESULT cakes]
            [COMMAND Initialize chips to an empty list, chip_rows to a list of R zeros, chip_cols to a list of C zeros, and chips_cnt to 0. RESULT chips,chip_rows,chip_cols,chips_cnt]
            [COMMAND For each row i from 0 to R-1 inclusive and each column j from 0 to C-1 inclusive, if cakes[i][j] equals '@', increment chips_cnt by 1, chip_rows[i] by 1, and chip_cols[j] by 1. RESULT chips_cnt,chip_rows,chip_cols]
            [COMMAND If chips_cnt equals 0, print 'Case #{}: POSSIBLE' with kase substituted for {} and return from the function immediately. RESULT printed_message]
            [COMMAND Compute parts as (H + 1) * (V + 1). RESULT parts]
            [COMMAND If chips_cnt modulo parts is not 0, print 'Case #{}: IMPOSSIBLE' with kase substituted for {} and return from the function immediately. RESULT printed_message]
            [COMMAND Compute piece_chip as the integer quotient of chips_cnt divided by parts; compute rows_chips as piece_chip * (V + 1); compute cols_chips as piece_chip * (H + 1); initialize hcuts to [0], vcuts to [0], and chips_row_cnt to 0. RESULT piece_chip,rows_chips,cols_chips,hcuts,vcuts,chips_row_cnt]
            [COMMAND For each row i from 0 to R-1 inclusive, add chip_rows[i] to chips_row_cnt; if chips_row_cnt is less than rows_chips, continue to the next row; if chips_row_cnt equals rows_chips, reset chips_row_cnt to 0 and append i + 1 to hcuts; if chips_row_cnt exceeds rows_chips, print 'Case #{}: IMPOSSIBLE' with kase substituted for {} and return from the function immediately. RESULT hcuts,chips_row_cnt]
            [COMMAND Initialize chips_col_cnt to 0. RESULT chips_col_cnt]
            [COMMAND For each column i from 0 to C-1 inclusive, add chip_cols[i] to chips_col_cnt; if chips_col_cnt is less than cols_chips, continue to the next column; if chips_col_cnt equals cols_chips, reset chips_col_cnt to 0 and append i + 1 to vcuts; if chips_col_cnt exceeds cols_chips, print 'Case #{}: IMPOSSIBLE' with kase substituted for {} and return from the function immediately. RESULT vcuts,chips_col_cnt]
            [COMMAND For each horizontal segment x from 0 to H-1 inclusive, append an empty row to chips; then for each vertical segment y from 0 to V-1 inclusive, set chips[x][y] to 0, count every '@' in rows hcuts[x] through hcuts[x+1]-1 and columns vcuts[y] through vcuts[y+1]-1, and if the resulting count is not equal to piece_chip, print 'Case #{}: IMPOSSIBLE' with kase substituted for {} and return from the function immediately. RESULT chips]
            [COMMAND After all rectangles have been verified, print 'Case #{}: POSSIBLE' with kase substituted for {} and return from the function. RESULT printed_message]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
